title: A reason should be provided when skipping a test
description: When skipping a test using decorators like @pytest.mark.skip or @unittest.skip, a reason should always be provided. This helps other developers understand why the test is disabled and under what circumstances it should be re-enabled. Without a reason, it becomes difficult to maintain the test suite and track technical debt.
message: Provide a reason when skipping this test.
impact: Test maintenance becomes difficult when skipped tests lack explanations. Developers cannot determine if tests should be re-enabled or remain disabled, leading to technical debt accumulation and potential gaps in test coverage.
recommendation: Always provide a meaningful reason when skipping tests. Use @pytest.mark.skip(reason='...') or @unittest.skip('...') with a clear explanation of why the test is skipped and when it might be re-enabled.

noncompliant.description: Tests are skipped without providing reasons, making maintenance difficult.

compliant.description: Tests provide clear reasons for why they are skipped.

why_is_this_an_issue: Skipping tests without providing a reason makes it difficult for developers to understand why the test was disabled. This can lead to confusion about whether the test should be re-enabled, fixed, or permanently removed, ultimately affecting code maintainability and test suite health.
how_to_fix: Add a descriptive reason parameter to skip decorators. For pytest: use @pytest.mark.skip(reason='explanation'). For unittest: use @unittest.skip('explanation'). The reason should explain why the test is skipped and ideally when it should be addressed.
